title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC being before sinning; generative presupposed
pass_a_gloss: If sinning follows being (non-beings have no accidents), the generative act is how we first are, and the act that first makes us sinners should follow and rest on it; at least it cannot make us sinners except through that prior act. Sinning presupposes being; in nature's order we become before we become sinners. So if we are sinners by another's imputed sin made ours, that imputation must follow something by which we were already human—subject before accident.
pass_b_english: For if sinning follows being, as it certainly ought (for of what is not there are no accidents), the act of generating is that by whose force we first are; this ought to seem to follow, and in it to be founded that act by whose force we first are sinners; at least this does not make us sinners except by means of that: and so it presupposes it: for to sin presupposes to be, and prior in the order of nature is that we become than that we become sinners. If therefore we were sinners by imputation of another's sin which becomes ours, that imputation ought to follow something by which we were humans, seeing that in nature's order we are humans before we are sinners, and the subject is prior to its accident.
source_text: Nam si peccare sequitur esse, ut certe debet (non entis enim non sunt accidentia) actus generandi is est cuius vi primum sumus, hunc sequi debere videtur, & in eo fundari is actus cuius vi primum peccatores sumus; saltem hic nos non facit peccatores, nisi illo mediante: itaque illum praesupponit: peccare enim praesupponit esse, & prius est naturae ordine nos fieri, quam fieri peccatores. Si ergo fuimus peccatores imputatione alieni peccati quae fit nostrum, ea imputatio sequi debet aliquid quo fuimus homines, siquidem ordine naturae prius sumus homines quam peccatores, prius est subjectum quam eius accidens.

choices.choice: Sinning presupposes being; human subject before imputed accident
